## Objective
- Build a complete, playable turn-based game about becoming the greatest necromancer of all time.

## Requirements
- Build immediately without clarification; make reasonable assumptions and note them when finished.
- For visual checks, save a small JPEG at a viewport no wider than 1280px and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Built a standalone, single-file browser game: tactical grid combat across four expeditions, with summoning, spells, leveling, progression, and local saves.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented the game UI and mechanics in `index.html`.
- Checked JavaScript syntax and opened the game in Playwright.
- Tested the intro and skeleton-summoning interaction.
- Saved and inspected `screenshots/gravebound.jpg` at 1280px viewport width.
- Added a data-URI favicon after noticing a missing favicon request.

### Active
- (none)

### Blocked
- Full expedition/combat progression has not been tested end-to-end.

## Next Move
1. If continuing development, test combat turns, defeat/victory transitions, persistence, and mobile layout in-browser.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Complete game implementation.
- `screenshots/gravebound.jpg`: Latest visual-check screenshot.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `git status --short` showed `index.html` and several repository files as untracked.
- A local HTTP server was started with `python3 -m http.server 3002`; Playwright opened `http://localhost:3002`.

playwright-cli - run playwright mcp commands from terminal

Usage: playwright-cli <command> [args] [options]
Usage: playwright-cli -s=<session> <command> [args] [options]

Core:
  open [url]                  open the browser
  attach [name]               attach to a running playwright browser
  close                       close the browser
  detach                      detach from an attached browser
  goto <url>                  navigate to a url
  type <text>                 type text into editable element
  click <target> [button]     perform click on a web page
  dblclick <target> [button]  perform double click on a web page
  fill <target> <text>        fill text into editable element
  drag <startTarget> <endTarget> perform drag and drop between two elements
  drop <target>               drop files or data onto an element
  hover <target>              hover over element on page
  select <target> <val>       select an option in a dropdown
  upload <files...>           upload one or multiple files
  check <target>              check a checkbox or radio button
  uncheck <target>            uncheck a checkbox or radio button
  snapshot [target]           capture page snapshot to obtain element ref
  find [text]                 search the page snapshot for text or a regexp, returning matching nodes with surrounding context (like search snippets)
  eval <func> [target]        evaluate javascript expression on page or element
  dialog-accept [prompt]      accept a dialog
  dialog-dismiss              dismiss a dialog
  resize <w> <h>              resize the browser window
  delete-data                 delete session data

Navigation:
  go-back                     go back to the previous page
  go-forward                  go forward to the next page
  reload                      reload the current page

Keyboard:
  press <key>                 press a key on the keyboard, `a`, `arrowleft`
  keydown <key>               press a key down on the keyboard
  keyup <key>                 press a key up on the keyboard

Mouse:
  mousemove <x> <y>           move mouse to a given position
  mousedown [button]          press mouse down
  mouseup [button]            press mouse up
  mousewheel <dx> <dy>        scroll mouse wheel

Save as:
  screenshot [target]         screenshot of the current page or element
  pdf                         save page as pdf

Tabs:
  tab-list                    list all tabs
  tab-new [url]               create a new tab
  tab-close [index]           close a browser tab
  tab-select <index>          select a browser tab

Storage:
  state-load <filename>       loads browser storage (authentication) state from a file
  state-save [filename]       saves the current storage (authentication) state to a file
  cookie-list                 list all cookies (optionally filtered by domain/path)
  cookie-get <name>           get a specific cookie by name
  cookie-set <name> <value>   set a cookie with optional flags
  cookie-delete <name>        delete a specific cookie
  cookie-clear                clear all cookies
  localstorage-list           list all localstorage key-value pairs
  localstorage-get <key>      get a localstorage item by key
  localstorage-set <key> <value> set a localstorage item
  localstorage-delete <key>   delete a localstorage item
  localstorage-clear          clear all localstorage
  sessionstorage-list         list all sessionstorage key-value pairs
  sessionstorage-get <key>    get a sessionstorage item by key
  sessionstorage-set <key> <value> set a sessionstorage item
  sessionstorage-delete <key> delete a sessionstorage item
  sessionstorage-clear        clear all sessionstorage

Network:
  requests                    list all network requests since loading the page. each request is numbered for use with the `request` command.
  request <index>             show full details (headers, body, response) of a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  request-headers <index>     print only the request headers for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  request-body <index>        print only the request body for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  response-headers <index>    print only the response headers for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  response-body <index>       print the response body for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command. textual bodies are inlined; binary bodies are saved to a file and the path is printed.
  route <pattern>             mock network requests matching a url pattern
  route-list                  list all active network routes
  unroute [pattern]           remove routes matching a pattern (or all routes)
  network-state-set <state>   set the browser network state to online or offline

DevTools:
  console [min-level]         list console messages
  run-code [code]             run playwright code snippet
  recording-start             start recording user actions
  recording-stop              stop recording user actions and print them as playwright code
  tracing-start               start trace recording
  tracing-stop                stop trace recording
  video-start [filename]      start video recording

Usage: playwright-cli <command> [args] [options]
Usage: playwright-cli -s=<session> <command> [args] [options]

Core:
  open [url]                  open the browser
  attach [name]               attach to a running playwright browser
  close                       close the browser
  detach                      detach from an attached browser
  goto <url>                  navigate to a url
  type <text>                 type text into editable element
  click <target> [button]     perform click on a web page
  dblclick <target> [button]  perform double click on a web page
  fill <target> <text>        fill text into editable element
  drag <startTarget> <endTarget> perform drag and drop between two elements
  drop <target>               drop files or data onto an element
  hover <target>              hover over element on page
  select <target> <val>       select an option in a dropdown
  upload <files...>           upload one or multiple files
  check <target>              check a checkbox or radio button
  uncheck <target>            uncheck a checkbox or radio button
  snapshot [target]           capture page snapshot to obtain element ref
  find [text]                 search the page snapshot for text or a regexp, returning matching nodes with surrounding context (like search snippets)
  eval <func> [target]        evaluate javascript expression on page or element
  dialog-accept [prompt]      accept a dialog
  dialog-dismiss              dismiss a dialog
  resize <w> <h>              resize the browser window
  delete-data                 delete session data

Navigation:
  go-back                     go back to the previous page
  go-forward                  go forward to the next page
  reload                      reload the current page

Keyboard:
  press <key>                 press a key on the keyboard, `a`, `arrowleft`
  keydown <key>               press a key down on the keyboard
  keyup <key>                 press a key up on the keyboard

Mouse:
  mousemove <x> <y>           move mouse to a given position
  mousedown [button]          press mouse down
  mouseup [button]            press mouse up
  mousewheel <dx> <dy>        scroll mouse wheel

Save as:
  screenshot [target]         screenshot of the current page or element
  pdf                         save page as pdf

Tabs:
  tab-list                    list all tabs
  tab-new [url]               create a new tab
  tab-close [index]           close a browser tab
  tab-select <index>          select a browser tab

Storage:
  state-load <filename>       loads browser storage (authentication) state from a file
  state-save [filename]       saves the current storage (authentication) state to a file
  cookie-list                 list all cookies (optionally filtered by domain/path)
  cookie-get <name>           get a specific cookie by name
  cookie-set <name> <value>   set a cookie with optional flags
  cookie-delete <name>        delete a specific cookie
  cookie-clear                clear all cookies
  localstorage-list           list all localstorage key-value pairs
  localstorage-get <key>      get a localstorage item by key
  localstorage-set <key> <value> set a localstorage item
  localstorage-delete <key>   delete a localstorage item
  localstorage-clear          clear all localstorage
  sessionstorage-list         list all sessionstorage key-value pairs
  sessionstorage-get <key>    get a sessionstorage item by key
  sessionstorage-set <key> <value> set a sessionstorage item
  sessionstorage-delete <key> delete a sessionstorage item
  sessionstorage-clear        clear all sessionstorage

Network:
  requests                    list all network requests since loading the page. each request is numbered for use with the `request` command.
  request <index>             show full details (headers, body, response) of a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  request-headers <index>     print only the request headers for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  request-body <index>        print only the request body for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  response-headers <index>    print only the response headers for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  response-body <index>       print the response body for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command. textual bodies are inlined; binary bodies are saved to a file and the path is printed.
  route <pattern>             mock network requests matching a url pattern
  route-list                  list all active network routes
  unroute [pattern]           remove routes matching a pattern (or all routes)
  network-state-set <state>   set the browser network state to online or offline

DevTools:
  console [min-level]         list console messages

  recording-stop              stop recording user actions and print them as playwright code
  tracing-start               start trace recording

  video-start [filename]      start video recording
  video-stop                  stop video recording
  video-chapter <title>       add a chapter marker to the video recording

Install:

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable turn-based game about becoming the greatest necromancer of all time.

## Requirements
- Build without clarification; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finished.
- For visual checks, save a small JPEG at a viewport no wider than 1280px and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Implemented a standalone, single-file browser game: tactical grid combat across four expeditions, with summoning, spells, leveling, progression, and local saves.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented the game UI and mechanics in `index.html`.
- Fixed enemy targeting: stage enemies now receive `type: 'enemy'`, and saved enemies are normalized during load.
- Verified JavaScript syntax, skeleton summoning, ally selection, movement, enemy turns, Bone Bolt targeting/damage, and New run reset.
- Saved and inspected `screenshots/gravebound.jpg` at 1280px viewport width; added a data-URI favicon.

### Active
- Continue testing full expedition progression, defeat/victory transitions, save restoration, and mobile layout.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Test combat through stage transitions, defeat/victory, and save restoration.
2. Check mobile layout and fix any issues found.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Complete game implementation.
- `screenshots/gravebound.jpg`: Latest visual-check screenshot.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `git status --short` previously listed `.gitignore`, `Agents.md`, `capture.sh`, `index.html`, `start.sh`, and `startup.sh` as untracked.
- Local HTTP server was started with `python3 -m http.server 3002`; Playwright tested `http://localhost:3002`.
- The current browser session has a test save with a single Grave Warden at 3 HP, Morwen adjacent, and the intro overlay visible; this is test state, not a clean game state.

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable turn-based game about becoming the greatest necromancer of all time.

## Requirements
- Build without clarification; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finished.
- For visual checks, save a small JPEG at a viewport no wider than 1280px and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Implemented a standalone, single-file browser game: tactical grid combat across four expeditions, with summoning, spells, leveling, progression, and local saves.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented the game UI and mechanics in `index.html`.
- Fixed enemy targeting by assigning enemies `type: 'enemy'` and normalizing saved enemies on load.
- Verified JavaScript syntax, skeleton summoning, ally selection, movement, enemy turns, Bone Bolt damage, and New run reset.
- Saved and inspected `screenshots/gravebound.jpg` at 1280px viewport width; added a data-URI favicon.
- Added initialization logic to preserve saved victory/defeat states, hide the intro for saved runs, and show victory details through a reusable `showVictory()` function.

### Active
- Verify expedition progression and victory/defeat transitions, including restoration of terminal states after reload.
- Check save restoration and mobile layout; fix issues found.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Retest victory and defeat with controlled saves, then verify progression between expeditions and reload restoration.
2. Check the game at mobile viewport sizes and correct any layout issues.
3. Save and inspect a current screenshot if visual changes are made.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Complete game implementation.
- `screenshots/gravebound.jpg`: Previously inspected visual-check screenshot.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `git status --short` previously listed `.gitignore`, `Agents.md`, `capture.sh`, `index.html`, `start.sh`, and `startup.sh` as untracked.
- Local HTTP server was started with `python3 -m http.server 3002`; Playwright tested `http://localhost:3002`.
- A controlled lethal Bone Bolt produced the victory overlay and set `mode: "victory"`, but reloading afterward showed `mode: "play"` with two enemies. The subsequent initialization change passed JavaScript syntax checking, but terminal-state restoration remains unverified.

1: ## Process lifecycle
2: 
3: - Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
4: - Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
5: - After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.
6: 
7: ## Linux browser and WebGPU capture
8: 
9: - Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
10: - Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
11: - Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
12: - Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
13: - Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
14: - Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
15: - Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
16: - Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
17: - Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.
18: 
19: ## Mobile browser games
20: 
21: - Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
22: - Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
23: - Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
24: - Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

playwright-cli - run playwright mcp commands from terminal

Usage: playwright-cli <command> [args] [options]
Usage: playwright-cli -s=<session> <command> [args] [options]

Core:
  open [url]                  open the browser
  attach [name]               attach to a running playwright browser
  close                       close the browser
  detach                      detach from an attached browser
  goto <url>                  navigate to a url
  type <text>                 type text into editable element
  click <target> [button]     perform click on a web page
  dblclick <target> [button]  perform double click on a web page
  fill <target> <text>        fill text into editable element
  drag <startTarget> <endTarget> perform drag and drop between two elements
  drop <target>               drop files or data onto an element
  hover <target>              hover over element on page
  select <target> <val>       select an option in a dropdown
  upload <files...>           upload one or multiple files
  check <target>              check a checkbox or radio button
  uncheck <target>            uncheck a checkbox or radio button
  snapshot [target]           capture page snapshot to obtain element ref
  find [text]                 search the page snapshot for text or a regexp, returning matching nodes with surrounding context (like search snippets)
  eval <func> [target]        evaluate javascript expression on page or element
  dialog-accept [prompt]      accept a dialog
  dialog-dismiss              dismiss a dialog
  resize <w> <h>              resize the browser window
  delete-data                 delete session data

Navigation:
  go-back                     go back to the previous page
  go-forward                  go forward to the next page
  reload                      reload the current page

Keyboard:
  press <key>                 press a key on the keyboard, `a`, `arrowleft`
  keydown <key>               press a key down on the keyboard
  keyup <key>                 press a key up on the keyboard

Mouse:
  mousemove <x> <y>           move mouse to a given position
  mousedown [button]          press mouse down
  mouseup [button]            press mouse up
  mousewheel <dx> <dy>        scroll mouse wheel

Save as:
  screenshot [target]         screenshot of the current page or element
  pdf                         save page as pdf

Tabs:
  tab-list                    list all tabs
  tab-new [url]               create a new tab
  tab-close [index]           close a browser tab
  tab-select <index>          select a browser tab

Storage:
  state-load <filename>       loads browser storage (authentication) state from a file
  state-save [filename]       saves the current storage (authentication) state to a file
  cookie-list                 list all cookies (optionally filtered by domain/path)
  cookie-get <name>           get a specific cookie by name
  cookie-set <name> <value>   set a cookie with optional flags
  cookie-delete <name>        delete a specific cookie
  cookie-clear                clear all cookies
  localstorage-list           list all localstorage key-value pairs
  localstorage-get <key>      get a localstorage item by key
  localstorage-set <key> <value> set a localstorage item
  localstorage-delete <key>   delete a localstorage item
  localstorage-clear          clear all localstorage
  sessionstorage-list         list all sessionstorage key-value pairs
  sessionstorage-get <key>    get a sessionstorage item by key
  sessionstorage-set <key> <value> set a sessionstorage item
  sessionstorage-delete <key> delete a sessionstorage item
  sessionstorage-clear        clear all sessionstorage

Network:
  requests                    list all network requests since loading the page. each request is numbered for use with the `request` command.
  request <index>             show full details (headers, body, response) of a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  request-headers <index>     print only the request headers for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  request-body <index>        print only the request body for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  response-headers <index>    print only the response headers for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  response-body <index>       print the response body for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command. textual bodies are inlined; binary bodies are saved to a file and the path is printed.
  route <pattern>             mock network requests matching a url pattern
  route-list                  list all active network routes
  unroute [pattern]           remove routes matching a pattern (or all routes)
  network-state-set <state>   set the browser network state to online or offline

DevTools:
  console [min-level]         list console messages
  run-code [code]             run playwright code snippet
  recording-start             start recording user actions
  recording-stop              stop recording user actions and print them as playwright code
  tracing-start               start trace recording
  tracing-stop                stop trace recording
  video-start [filename]      start video recording
  video-stop                  stop video recording

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Complete and validate a playable turn-based necromancer game with tactical combat, four expeditions, local saves, and randomized gameplay-altering boon choices.

## Requirements
- Make reasonable assumptions without clarification.
- For visual checks, save a small JPEG at a viewport no wider than 1280px and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Implement the standalone browser game in `index.html`, with tactical grid combat and persisted saves.
- Offer one of three randomized boons after each non-final expedition victory.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented spells, summoning, leveling, expeditions, local saves, and restoration of victory/defeat states after reload.
- Fixed mobile layout overflow at 320px and verified layouts at 320px and 390px.
- Added three randomized boon choices after non-final victories, with reward choices and boon state persisted.
- Added eight boon effects and displayed claimed boons in the sidebar.

Usage: playwright-cli <command> [args] [options]
Usage: playwright-cli -s=<session> <command> [args] [options]

Core:
  open [url]                  open the browser
  attach [name]               attach to a running playwright browser
  close                       close the browser
  detach                      detach from an attached browser
  goto <url>                  navigate to a url
  type <text>                 type text into editable element
  click <target> [button]     perform click on a web page
  dblclick <target> [button]  perform double click on a web page
  fill <target> <text>        fill text into editable element
  drag <startTarget> <endTarget> perform drag and drop between two elements
  drop <target>               drop files or data onto an element
  hover <target>              hover over element on page
  select <target> <val>       select an option in a dropdown
  upload <files...>           upload one or multiple files
  check <target>              check a checkbox or radio button
  uncheck <target>            uncheck a checkbox or radio button
  snapshot [target]           capture page snapshot to obtain element ref
  find [text]                 search the page snapshot for text or a regexp, returning matching nodes with surrounding context (like search snippets)
  eval <func> [target]        evaluate javascript expression on page or element
  dialog-accept [prompt]      accept a dialog
  dialog-dismiss              dismiss a dialog
  resize <w> <h>              resize the browser window

Navigation:

  go-forward                  go forward to the next page

Keyboard:
  press <key>                 press a key on the keyboard, `a`, `arrowleft`
  keydown <key>               press a key down on the keyboard
  keyup <key>                 press a key up on the keyboard

Mouse:
  mousemove <x> <y>           move mouse to a given position
  mousedown [button]          press mouse down
  mouseup [button]            press mouse up
  mousewheel <dx> <dy>        scroll mouse wheel

Save as:
  screenshot [target]         screenshot of the current page or element

Tabs:

Storage:

  state-save [filename]       saves the current storage (authentication) state to a file
  cookie-list                 list all cookies (optionally filtered by domain/path)

  cookie-set <name> <value>   set a cookie with optional flags
  cookie-delete <name>        delete a specific cookie

  localstorage-list           list all localstorage key-value pairs
  localstorage-get <key>      get a localstorage item by key

Network:

  request <index>             show full details (headers, body, response) of a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  request-headers <index>     print only the request headers for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  request-body <index>        print only the request body for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  response-headers <index>    print only the response headers for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  response-body <index>       print the response body for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command. textual bodies are inlined; binary bodies are saved to a file and the path is printed.
  route <pattern>             mock network requests matching a url pattern

DevTools:
  console [min-level]         list console messages

  recording-stop              stop recording user actions and print them as playwright code
  tracing-start               start trace recording

  video-stop                  stop video recording
  video-chapter <title>       add a chapter marker to the video recording
  video-show-actions          annotate subsequent cli/mcp actions on the page with a callout that names the action and highlights the target element
  video-hide-actions          stop annotating actions performed on the page

  highlight [target]          show (or with --hide, remove) a highlight overlay for an element; `--hide` without a target hides all page highlights.

Install:
  install                     initialize workspace
  install-browser [browser]   install browser

Browser sessions:
  list                        list browser sessions

  kill-all                    forcefully kill all browser sessions (for stale/zombie processes)

Global options:
  --help [command]            print help

  --version                   print version

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Improve the existing playable necromancer game with autonomous friendly minions, more summoned-undead variety, additional levels, and a more appealing visual design.

## Requirements
- “Friendly Minions should act on their own.”
- “There needs to variety to summoned undead.”
- “Add more levels.”
- “Make it more aesthetically pleasing”

## Decisions
- Expanded the campaign design to eight expeditions, ending with The Throne of Bones.
- Added three summon types: Skeleton, Ghoul, and Wraith, with different costs, stats, and ranges.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added four new expedition names, descriptions, and enemy groups to `index.html`.
- Added summon choices for Skeletons, Ghouls, and Wraiths.
- Updated expedition display to show eight stages and dynamically render campaign progress.
- Updated intro instructions to describe autonomous undead and the expanded campaign.

### Active
- Implement autonomous minion turns; summons currently still share player-controlled turns.
- Finish updating all progression and victory logic for eight stages.
- Improve visual design.
- Validate gameplay, progression, responsive layout, and browser console.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect remaining hardcoded four-stage checks in `index.html`, including `showVictory()` and `continueRun()`, and update them for eight stages.
2. Implement autonomous minion behavior each round and ensure players can only directly command Morwen.
3. Review summon action and minion selection/turn flow for inconsistencies.
4. Refine the visual design, then run syntax and gameplay checks.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Standalone game implementation; active changes to stages, campaign UI, and summon choices are here.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; the working tree previously showed `.gitignore`, `Agents.md`, `capture.sh`, `index.html`, `start.sh`, and `startup.sh` as untracked.
- The eight-stage definitions and summon variants are present, but remaining logic still includes checks such as `S.stage===3` and `S.stage<3`, so progression is incomplete.
- Minions are still selectable and their action buttons remain player-controlled; autonomous turns have not been implemented.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Improve the playable necromancer game with autonomous friendly minions, varied summons, an eight-expedition campaign, and more appealing visuals.

## Requirements
- Friendly Minions should act on their own.
- Summoned undead should have variety.
- Add more levels and improve the game’s visual appeal.

## Decisions
- The campaign has eight expeditions, ending with The Throne of Bones.
- Summon options are Skeleton, Ghoul, and Wraith, with distinct costs, stats, and ranges.

## Work State
### Completed
- Expanded the campaign enemy and stage definitions to eight expeditions.
- Added Skeleton, Ghoul, and Wraith summon choices.
- Updated campaign display and expedition count for eight stages.
- Prevented direct selection of friendly minions; added autonomous minion movement and attacks at the start of the enemy turn.
- Updated victory and continuation checks to use the final campaign stage.

### Active
- Refine visual design.
- Validate campaign progression, summon and minion behavior, responsive layout, and browser console.
- Review edge cases in autonomous combat and remaining stage-dependent UI/progression logic.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect and test autonomous minion turns, including attacks that clear the final enemy before enemy actions proceed.
2. Check for remaining stale hardcoded campaign values or mismatches in stage rewards and UI.
3. Improve visual design and responsive behavior.
4. Run syntax and gameplay checks; review browser console output.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Standalone game implementation; campaign, summons, turn flow, and visuals are here.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; previously reported untracked files included `.gitignore`, `Agents.md`, `capture.sh`, `index.html`, `start.sh`, and `startup.sh`.
- The minion turn now runs inside `endTurn()` before `enemyTurn()`. Review its interactions with victory handling and enemy-turn flow.

- Improve the playable necromancer game with autonomous friendly minions, varied summons, an eight-expedition campaign, and more appealing visuals.
- Validate campaign progression, combat behavior, and responsive presentation.

- Friendly minions should act autonomously.
- Summoned undead should have distinct types.

- The campaign has eight expeditions, ending with The Throne of Bones.

- Expanded campaign stages and enemies to eight expeditions; updated campaign count, labels, and final-stage checks.

- Improved minion pathfinding to find routes around obstacles toward attack range.

- (none)

- `index.html`: Standalone game implementation; campaign, summons, turn flow, pathfinding, and visuals.

## Objective
- Make the existing necromancer game more engaging, with deeper gameplay and clearer, satisfying feedback for summons and combat.

## Requirements
- The game currently feels basic and lacks meaningful feedback.
- Summons should have distinct special effects that players can notice; the user asks, “Where's the fun”

## Decisions
- Earlier implementation uses three summon types—Skeleton, Ghoul, and Wraith—with different costs, stats, and ranges, but their special gameplay effects and feedback remain insufficient.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented and browser-validated an eight-expedition campaign, autonomous minion combat, three summon types, and visual refinements in `index.html`.
- Verified campaign transitions, last-foe minion kills, responsive layouts from 320 to 1440 px, and no browser console errors.

### Active
- Redesign or deepen moment-to-moment gameplay so summon types have distinct, understandable abilities and combat provides satisfying feedback.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect the current game flow in `index.html` and decide on concrete, differentiated summon abilities and tactical choices.
2. Implement noticeable combat feedback, such as clear action animations, hit/damage cues, and combat log messaging, while keeping the game playable and understandable.
3. Validate the new abilities and feedback in a browser and confirm campaign progression and responsive layouts still work.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Standalone game implementation, combat, summons, campaign, UI, and visual styling.
- `/tmp/opencode/gravebound-check.cjs`: Browser harness for summon behavior, combat, campaign progression, and responsive geometry.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `git status --short` showed `.gitignore`, `Agents.md`, `capture.sh`, `index.html`, `start.sh`, and `startup.sh` as untracked.
- Previous validation screenshot: `/tmp/opencode/gravebound-final.png`.
- The last user feedback requests a substantive improvement to game depth and fun; no new gameplay design has yet been implemented.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Make the necromancer game more engaging, with distinct summon abilities and clearer, more satisfying combat feedback.

## Requirements
- Summons should have noticeable special effects; the game should feel deeper than simply summoning monsters.

## Decisions
- Skeletons guard nearby allies, reducing incoming damage by 1.
- Ghouls deal bonus damage to wounded foes and heal themselves when feasting.
- Wraiths attack at range and steal 1 essence on hit.
- Combat feedback includes hit animations, floating damage and ability cues, summon descriptions, and combat-log messages.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented summon abilities and feedback in `index.html`.
- Validated summon behavior, autonomous combat, last-foe kills, all eight campaign transitions, responsive layouts from 320 to 1440 px, and no browser console errors.

### Active
- (none)

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Get user feedback on the updated gameplay and decide whether further depth or polish is needed.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Standalone game implementation, summon abilities, combat feedback, campaign, and UI.
- `/tmp/opencode/gravebound-check.cjs`: Browser harness for summon behavior, campaign progression, and responsive geometry.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `git status --short` shows `.gitignore`, `Agents.md`, `capture.sh`, `index.html`, `start.sh`, and `startup.sh` as untracked.
- Browser validation completed with `node /tmp/opencode/gravebound-check.cjs`; screenshot saved to `/tmp/opencode/gravebound-final.png`.
